regional_assessment: East Asian monsoon regime exhibits strong north-south thermal gradients and high interannual rainfall variability. Calibration data (2003-2016) indicates frequent low-temperature stress (tmin q05: -7.8°C) and precipitation deficits (prec q25: 0.037 mm/day), while historical CSV records (2001-2016) reveal extreme hydrological variance (dry_days median: 306 vs wet_days median: 59) and distinct regimes (cool_wet vs hot_dry). Residual stress evidence is unavailable, necessitating reliance on calibration event thresholds for daily event detection and CSV regime frequency for broad climate classification.

candidates.agronomic_rationale: Calibration-only profile (2003-2016) provides direct thresholds for daily stress events observed during the maize growing season. It captures the frequency of frost (tmin < 0°C) and drought (prec < 1 mm) conditions prevalent in the calibration set, ensuring event detection aligns with the specific climatic reality of the 31 locations studied.

Structured CSV records (2001-2016) define broad climate regimes (cool_wet, hot_dry, long_dry_spell) without yield labels. This configuration uses CSV-derived annual aggregates (e.g., frost_days, gdd10_c_day) to classify years into these regimes, enabling the assessment of temperature and water limitation frequency across the monsoon gradient.

Hybrid approach combines calibration daily event thresholds (prec < 0.037 mm, tmin < -7.8°C) with CSV annual regime metrics (frost_days, max_consecutive_dry_days) to address the lack of residual stress evidence. It uses calibration extremes for daily stress triggers and CSV medians for robust annual regime aggregation.
